[06-09-2024]
[Upgrade Workflow]
1. Code changes for upgrade workflow are being tested on PG DB Server VMs
2. The permissions suggested by logging FEAT are not working for Upgrade  workflow and post-upgrade, we are seeing failures for backup operations.
3. We are increasing the permissions from base (used by logging FEAT) to make NDB functionalities work with only required permissions keeping world-writable removed.
4. Based on testing, Folder: 755, Executable Files: 750, Non-executable Files: 644 and 3rd Party Software: Remove write for "Others", is working. Note here some of the files/folders owned by database user are still having world-writable permission (666 in this case)
5. Next step is to check on reducing permissions for user other than NDB user.

[Deployment Workflow]
The Code changes are done for deployment scenario and are yet to be testing. Testing will be done once upgrade workflow is tested.

[Registration Workflow]
We have identified places where we need to add code to set the permissions. Code changes will be once upgrade workflow is tested.

====================================

[02-09-2024]
1. Discussed the scope of the changes from Upgrade and Deployment Scenario with Akshay Chandak and Rahul Khandelwal
2. We are covering Control Plane VMs and Linux DB Server VMs
3. We are coving ERA_BASE directory on these VMs
4. We are following below permissions
     a. Folders: 750
     b. Executable Files: 750 (considering .sh files as executables)
     c. Non-executable Files: 640 (all files except executables)
     d. There is an exception for shippable python on DB Server VMs
                - We found that for python binaries in shippable python, we need execute permission for "other"
                - For all files/folders under shippable python on linux DB Server VMs, we will remove write permission for "other" so that these files/folders are not work writable, rest of the permissions for "owner" and "group" remains same to avoid breaking functionality of 3rd party software.
                 - E.g. We will change 666 permission to 664, 777 permission to 775 and 664 remains as is and 775 remains as is.
5. The changes are being done during Upgrade for control plane and linux DB Server VMs, Deployment of Control Plane VMs and creation of ERA_BASE directory on linux db server vms which can happen during provisioning/registration/clone/restore.

[06-09-2024]
[Upgrade Workflow]
1. Code changes for upgrade workflow are being tested on PG DB Server VMs
2. The permissions suggested by logging FEAT are not working for Upgrade  workflow and post-upgrade, we are seeing failures for backup operations.
3. We are increasing the permissions from base (used by logging FEAT) to make NDB functionalities work with only required permissions keeping world-writable removed.
4. Based on testing, Folder: 755, Executable Files: 750, Non-executable Files: 644 and 3rd Party Software: Remove write for "Others", is working. Note here some of the files/folders owned by database user are still having world-writable permission (666 in this case)
5. Next step is to check on reducing permissions for user other than NDB user.

[Deployment Workflow]
The Code changes are done for deployment scenario and are yet to be testing. Testing will be done once upgrade workflow is tested.

[Registration Workflow]
We have identified places where we need to add code to set the permissions. Code changes will be once upgrade workflow is tested.

====================================

[02-09-2024]
1. Discussed the scope of the changes from Upgrade and Deployment Scenario with Akshay Chandak and Rahul Khandelwal
2. We are covering Control Plane VMs and Linux DB Server VMs
3. We are coving ERA_BASE directory on these VMs
4. We are following below permissions
     a. Folders: 750
     b. Executable Files: 750 (considering .sh files as executables)
     c. Non-executable Files: 640 (all files except executables)
     d. There is an exception for shippable python on DB Server VMs
                - We found that for python binaries in shippable python, we need execute permission for "other"
                - For all files/folders under shippable python on linux DB Server VMs, we will remove write permission for "other" so that these files/folders are not work writable, rest of the permissions for "owner" and "group" remains same to avoid breaking functionality of 3rd party software.
                 - E.g. We will change 666 permission to 664, 777 permission to 775 and 664 remains as is and 775 remains as is.
5. The changes are being done during Upgrade for control plane and linux DB Server VMs, Deployment of Control Plane VMs and creation of ERA_BASE directory on linux db server vms which can happen during provisioning/registration/clone/restore.
